item.title: The science of deep sleep and how Duroflex Airboost helps you get more of it
item.description:
India’s newest sleep technology is designed to enhance the N3 stage, the body’s repair shift, for better recovery, immunity, and stress resilience.

item.content:encoded:
You can get enough sleep and still not get enough recovery.

We obsess over sleep duration, the “eight hours” metric, but duration alone doesn't tell the whole story. What matters just as much is depth. Deep sleep is the stage where the body does its heaviest lifting: repairing tissue, consolidating memory, and resetting the hormones that govern everything from appetite to stress. Yet for a growing number of people, deep sleep is the first thing to go missing, even when total sleep time looks normal on paper.

The different stages of sleep

Sleep isn't a single, uniform state. It cycles through distinct stages roughly every 90 minutes, each with a different job.

Light sleep (N1 and N2) acts as the transition zone; the body slows down, heart rate drops, and brain activity shifts into slower rhythms. This stage makes up the bulk of a typical night, but it's largely preparatory.

Deep sleep, or N3 stage (also called slow-wave sleep), is where the real restorative work happens. Brain waves slow dramatically, blood pressure and breathing reach their lowest points, and the body redirects energy toward physical repair, regenerating muscle, strengthening the immune system, and clearing metabolic waste from the brain.

Growth hormone release peaks during this stage, which is why it's often called the body's “repair shift”,

Rapid Eye Movement(REM) sleep stage follows, associated more with dreaming and cognitive processing than physical recovery.

Crucially, deep sleep is front-loaded into the first half of the night. If you go to bed late, cut sleep short, or microawake multiple times during your sleep, you disproportionately lose N3 stage, even if your total hours stay roughly the same.

When eight hours still isn’t enough

If you’re usually sleep-deprived, you don’t get to know it right away, since it doesn't show itself with obvious symptoms. Most of these symptoms are considered normal and ignorable, like sluggish mornings, feeling tired, and being unproductive.

But the sleep debt compounds, and it can affect your physical recovery, leading to muscle soreness, joint stiffness, and lingering fatigue. It can also affect your overall immunity, since much of the body’s repair and defence activity happens mostly during the N3 stage.

Without enough N3 stage in every sleep cycle, it becomes harder to regulate your hormones, including the balance of cortisol and growth hormone, which can affect stress resilience, appetite, and long-term metabolic health. Your cognitive sharpness also takes a hit, since deep sleep (N3 stage) also plays a role in clearing metabolic wastes from the brain overnight.

Heat discomfort, spinal misalignment, and micro-awakenings during the night can prevent the body from settling into and staying in N3, even across a full eight hours in bed.

Many people don’t realise that the frustrating part isn’t always how many hours you sleep, but how much of the right kind of sleep you’re actually getting.

Where Duroflex Airboost mattress comes in

Duroflex Airboost was engineered specifically to support quicker sleep onset and deeper sleep, positioning itself as India's newest sleep technology built around this problem.

Airboost is Duroflex's proprietary open-matrix mattress technology, built from over one lakh independently responsive fibres designed to improve airflow, movement response, and postural support.

Trusted by athletes around the world, this sleep technology is brought to Indiab for the first time by Duroflex. Airboost is accredited by the Indian Society for Sleep Research (ISSR) and recommended by doctors at the National Health Academy (NHA).

Three features built around deep sleep

1. Pressure relief from postural support

Rather than offering uniform support across the body, the mattress uses hyperlocal support built from over one lakh+ AirKnit fibres, distributing pressure according to the body's actual contours. You get the right kind of postural alignment for all types of sleepers as the individual fibres easily support every tiny pressure point across your body.

Misalignment and pressure build-up at the shoulders and hips are a common reason sleepers wake or shift position before completing a full deep-sleep cycle; proper medium-firm support like this addresses the issue at the source rather than masking it with extra foam cushioning.

2. An open-matrix core for breathability

Airboost features a 3D open-cell matrix made up of roughly 90% air, creating continuous airflow throughout the mattress that helps dissipate heat and sweat more effectively, keeping sleepers closer to a thermoneutral zone for cooler, deeper sleep. Airboost is 3X more breathable than traditional mattresses on the market.

Since body temperature naturally needs to drop to initiate and sustain deep sleep, a surface that actively supports heat dissipation removes one of the most common, and least discussed, barriers to N3 sleep.

3. Energy restoration

Each Airboost fibre responds instantly to the pressure placed on it, providing maximum rebound that makes turning and changing positions effortless. This way, the body’s energy is conserved for overnight recovery and you get to complete full sleep cycles without micro-awakenings.

Frequent, effortful repositioning is one of the quiet disruptors of deep sleep; every restless shift is a small pull away from the N3 stage. By minimizing these and micro-awakenings, this mattress helps the body stay in deep sleep for longer, uninterrupted stretches.

Airboost is accredited by the Indian Society for Sleep Research (ISSR) for delivering 30% more deep sleep(N3 stage), and is also recommended by doctors at the National Health Academy (NHA). Rather than treating sleep as one undifferentiated block of hours, their design specifically targets enhancement of N3 sleep, the stage most essential for physical repair, stronger immunity, and stress recovery.

Final thoughts

The conversation around sleep is shifting, from counting hours to increasing sleep stages. Deep sleep isn't a luxury metric; it's the mechanism behind physical recovery, immune resilience, and hormonal balance. As awareness grows, so does scrutiny of the products claiming to support it. Duroflex Airboost, a combination of engineered airflow, responsive movement support, and clinically backed deep-sleep enhancement, reflects a broader shift in the mattress category, one where design decisions are increasingly expected to be measured, not just marketed.

item.title: 5 Richard Osman quotes that reveal the human side of mystery
item.description: Explore five Richard Osman quotes that reveal how mysteries explore human nature, friendship, loneliness and the unexpected complexity of life.
item.content:encoded:
Mystery novels are often associated with murder, hidden clues, unexpected suspects and shocking revelations.

But the most memorable crime stories are not always about discovering who committed a crime. Sometimes, they are about understanding why people behave the way they do, what they hide from others and what they need most from life. British author Richard Osman explores these themes in his bestselling crime fiction, particularly The Thursday Murder Club.

The novel follows four older residents of a retirement community who investigate unsolved murders, bringing together suspense, humour, friendship and reflections on ageing.

What makes Osman's writing appealing is the way ordinary human experiences sit alongside extraordinary crimes. His characters have regrets, complicated relationships, personal ambitions and a deep desire to feel connected to others.

5 Richard Osman quotes that reveal the human side of mystery

1. “I know the difference between alone and lonely”

This line from The Thursday Murder Club captures an important distinction between solitude and loneliness.

Being alone does not necessarily mean feeling isolated. Some people genuinely enjoy their own company, while others can feel lonely even when surrounded by friends, family or colleagues.

The difference lies in whether solitude is a choice or an experience that leaves someone feeling disconnected. Osman's characters challenge the assumption that older people naturally become less interested in the world around them. They continue to seek companionship, excitement, intellectual stimulation and opportunities to make a difference.

The quote also reminds readers that meaningful relationships are not simply about having people nearby. They are about feeling understood, valued and included.

The takeaway: Loneliness is not always visible. A person can have a busy social life and still long for a deeper connection with someone who understands them.

2. “We all want to be chosen”

In The Thursday Murder Club, Osman explores the complicated relationship between choice, belonging and the desire to be wanted. The novel's reflections on this subject are collected among its widely shared quotations.

The desire to be chosen appears in many aspects of life. People want to be selected for opportunities, appreciated by friends, loved by partners and remembered by those who matter to them. Even people who appear independent may quietly wonder whether they are important to anyone else. This is one reason mysteries can be so emotionally engaging.

Beneath the investigation, characters may be struggling with rejection, insecurity, jealousy or the fear of becoming irrelevant. Their actions become easier to understand when readers look beyond the evidence and consider their emotional needs. Osman's characters demonstrate that the need for acceptance does not disappear with age. It remains part of being human, regardless of experience or social status.

The takeaway: Wanting to matter to someone is not a weakness. The important thing is to recognise your worth without allowing other people's approval to define it.

3. “Count the good days”

Osman's writing frequently balances the darker elements of crime fiction with observations about appreciating everyday life. In The Thursday Murder Club, this idea appears in a reflection about recognising good days and carrying their memories forward.

Crime stories often revolve around loss, uncertainty and the consequences of past decisions. Yet these difficult circumstances can make ordinary pleasures feel more meaningful. A conversation with a friend, a shared meal or a peaceful afternoon can become precious when life feels unpredictable.

The residents of Coopers Chase have lived long enough to understand that happiness does not always arrive through dramatic achievements.

Sometimes, it comes from small moments of companionship and the freedom to enjoy the present. This perspective gives Osman's mysteries an emotional depth that goes beyond solving crimes. Readers are encouraged to notice the good in their own lives rather than waiting for everything to become perfect.

The takeaway: Not every day needs to be extraordinary to be worthwhile. Learning to appreciate small moments can change how we remember our lives.

4. “Always look where the action isn't”

This observation from The Thursday Murder Club reflects the attention to detail that makes a good detective.

In a mystery, the most obvious suspect is not necessarily the person responsible. A convincing investigation requires looking beyond dramatic events and paying attention to the details that others overlook.

The same principle applies to understanding people. Someone's loudest reaction may not reveal their deepest concern, while a quiet change in behaviour can suggest that something important is happening beneath the surface.

Osman's approach to crime fiction places considerable emphasis on character.

In an interview with PBS Books, he explained that he begins with his characters and develops the murder plot around them. This approach encourages readers to become observers of human behaviour rather than simply followers of clues.

The takeaway: Important truths are not always found in the most obvious places. Sometimes, listening carefully and noticing what others miss can reveal more than making quick assumptions.

5. “Don't let it be in charge”

Osman's observations about everyday life also extend to money and the influence it can have on personal decisions. A short line from The Thursday Murder Club captures this idea: “Don't let it be in charge.”

Although the novel is a murder mystery, its characters encounter concerns that extend well beyond crime. Money, relationships, family responsibilities and personal independence all shape how people navigate the world.

Financial security can provide freedom and comfort, but the pursuit of money can also influence priorities, create conflict and complicate relationships. When material success becomes the only measure of achievement, other sources of happiness can be overlooked.

This theme also connects to the wider appeal of Osman's characters: they are not defined by a single ambition or social role. They have different motivations, values and ideas about what makes life meaningful.

The takeaway: Money can be an important tool, but it should not become the sole measure of a successful life. Personal relationships, peace of mind and a sense of purpose matter too.

Final thoughts

Richard Osman’s mysteries blend crime and humour with thoughtful insights into loneliness, friendship, ageing and belonging. The Thursday Murder Club resonates because its characters face familiar emotional struggles.

Ultimately, the human side of a mystery is what gives its revelations lasting meaning. Discovering who committed a crime may resolve the central puzzle, but understanding the people involved is what makes the story memorable.

item.title: How a FD calculator helps investors plan savings with ease
item.description:
Saving for life’s big goals? Start with an FD calculator
Bajaj Finance’s online tool lets you compare amounts, tenures, and payout options instantly, turning guesswork into clear savings plans.
Establishing a financial goal makes the process of saving a lot easier. If you plan to save well,
item.content:encoded:
Establishing a financial goal makes the process of saving a lot easier. If you plan to save well, you need to know the total amount you plan to save as well as the time frame for saving. Whether you want to save for a family event, pay for tuition, or renovate your home, you should be aware of the amount of money you want to save and the time frame.

A fixed deposit is a type of investment that guarantees you a fixed amount of return during the investment period. However, calculating returns manually can be a hassle. So, using Bajaj Finance's FD Calculator saves a lot of time and energy as it allows you to know your estimated returns in seconds based on your inputs. You can explore options before making the final investment.

Define your savings goal

The first crucial step in investing is to find out your investment's purpose. Knowing why you are making the investment will give you the desired amount you need to save and the time of retrieval for the money.

For example, if the amount required for a particular instance is Rs 3 lakh in three years, you can use the calculator

See how much your deposit may earn

The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator estimates your return after you provide the required inputs. These generally include the investment amount, investor category, tenure, and interest payout option.

The result shows the estimated interest earned and the expected maturity amount. This allows you to see how much of the final value comes from your original deposit and how much may come from interest.

The calculation also makes percentage rates easier to understand. An annual interest rate may appear attractive, but the calculator translates it into an estimated rupee value. This provides a more practical picture of how the investment could contribute towards your savings goal.

Choose an amount without affecting your budget

A larger amount will yield a higher maturity value, but putting in too much money could create issues when it's time to pay the bills. The right figure would give you the money you need to achieve your future goal.

Before making a fixed deposit, be sure to think about rent, bills, school tuition, medical expenses, and anything else that you must pay for in the near future.

The calculator allows you to compare various amounts almost instantly. Enter Rs 50,000, Rs 1 lakh, or any other amount and watch the maturity figure change accordingly.

Match the tenure with your goal date

Bajaj Finance’s fixed deposit scheme has time frames that range from 12 to 60 months. The applicable interest rate differs based on the time chosen, meaning changing the time can result in varied rates of return.

A longer period gives the deposit a longer opportunity to earn interest through the compound option, but maturity needs to happen close to the time of using the funds.

Suppose your goal is due after two years. Selecting a five-year deposit merely because it shows a larger maturity value could leave the funds unavailable at the required time. The FD interest Calculator lets you compare eligible tenures and select one that balances potential earnings with timely access.

How to use the FD calculator

The Bajaj Finance online calculator is designed to provide estimates quickly. You can repeat the calculation with different inputs and compare the results before starting the investment process.

  1. Choose the investor category: Select the relevant option for a customer below 60 or a senior citizen.
  2. Enter the deposit amount: Add the amount you are considering investing.
  3. Select the tenure: Choose an available period between 12 and 60 months.
  4. Pick the payout option: Select interest at maturity or a periodic payout frequency.
  5. Review the estimate: Check the estimated interest earnings and maturity amount.
  6. Try another combination: Change the amount, tenure, or payout option to compare the result.

Consider safety and access to your money

Return is only one aspect of FD planning. Credit ratings of the institution, conditions for early withdrawal, nomination facility, maturity instructions, and renewal options are some other aspects that must be evaluated as well.

Bajaj Finance Fixed Deposit comes with guaranteed returns and good credit safety ratings, with CRISIL AAA/STABLE and ICRA AAA (Stable). Minimum investment starts at Rs 15,000, making it possible to experiment with various amounts via the calculator before finalizing the exact amount.

Early withdrawals are allowed but require certain conditions to be met, which could lead to lower interest. Therefore, it is wise to select an amount and tenure you are fairly certain you will not deviate from.

Conclusion

Choosing the appropriate amount and period for a fixed deposit account can help you achieve short-term and medium-term savings objectives. The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator lets you know the returns that different fixed deposit accounts can bring.

It is useful to compare various investment scenarios involving the fixed deposit calculator and check information about current FD interest rates, tax rates, credit ratings, and penalties for early withdrawal of a fixed deposit.

item.title: From implementation to innovation: The next step in your Gemini Enterprise journey
item.description: Join Google Cloud's AI and ML experts for the second edition of the Gemini Enterprise series, covering app connectivity, identity management, and enterprise-grade security.
item.content:encoded:
How do you move from a basic Gemini Enterprise setup to a live, identity-aware, data-protected AI platform?

That is the question at the center of Google Cloud's next webinar, in partnership with YourStory. On October 23, Google Cloud's AI and ML experts return for the second edition of the Gemini Enterprise series, titled ‘Gemini Enterprise: Integrate, secure, and scale your AI strategy’.

Where the first series focused on initial setup, this session moves into the technical connectivity that determines whether a Gemini Enterprise deployment actually works inside an organization's existing ecosystem. Attendees will get a practical look at bridging Gemini Enterprise with the tools already in use, while maintaining the security and compliance standards enterprises cannot afford to skip.

Whether the challenge is navigating complex compliance requirements or automating workflows across multiple apps, the session is built to provide a clear roadmap for the next stage of the AI journey.

What attendees will learn

The session will open with a look at Workspace synergy, walking through how different Gemini Enterprise editions integrate with an organization's existing productivity suite to unlock more value from tools already in place.

From there, the focus will shift to app connectivity. Attendees will see how to securely link Gmail, Calendar, and Drive, allowing Gemini to reason over internal data and automate workflows that span multiple applications, rather than working in isolation.

The webinar will also cover identity and access, including a walkthrough of Workforce Identity Federation using providers like Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, to make identity management seamless across an enterprise's existing infrastructure.

Finally, the session aims to address security in depth, covering Safety Filters, AI Defense policies, and Model Armor, the tools organizations need to defend against prompt injection and protect personally identifiable information as AI usage scales.

Meet the speakers

The session aims to bring together specialists across connectivity, identity, and security.

Ria Patel, Platform Customer Engineer for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts at Google Cloud, opens with a walkthrough on connecting Google Calendar to Gemini Enterprise.

Janani Pandurangan, also a Platform Customer Engineer for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts, follows with a session on connecting Gemini Enterprise to Gmail.

Jared Houston, Security Customer Engineer at Google Cloud, covers connecting Google Drive to Gemini Enterprise.

Derian Tungka and Graciella Liander, both Platform Customer Engineers for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts, co-lead a deep dive into third-party identity provider integration, offering step-by-step guidance on Workforce Identity Federation using Okta or Microsoft Entra ID.

Methasit (Most) Tuwawit, Platform Customer Engineer for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts, leads a session on securing a Gemini Enterprise application.

Eva Gao, Security Customer Engineer at Google Cloud, closes the technical program with a session on Model Armor, covering prompt injection and data leakage prevention through Safety Filters and AI Defense policies.

Why this matters

For organizations past the initial pilot stage, the risks shift. It is no longer just about getting Gemini Enterprise running, but about making sure it connects securely to the systems that hold sensitive data, respects existing identity infrastructure, and holds up against the kinds of attacks that come with wider AI adoption, such as prompt injection and data leakage.

This webinar is built for that stage. Rather than a high-level overview, it offers specific, technical guidance from the engineers who work on these integrations directly, covering the connectivity and security groundwork that determines whether an AI deployment can scale safely across an organization.

Register now to secure your spot and learn how to take your Gemini Enterprise deployment from basic setup to a fully integrated, secure, enterprise-ready platform.

item.title: 5 Quotes from the book It Matters a Lot by Shubhra Saxena
item.description: Explore five thought-provoking quotes from Shubhra Saxena’s It Matters A Lot on success, happiness, ambition and finding meaning in life.
item.content:encoded:
We spend much of our lives working towards milestones that society considers important. Degrees, careers, financial security, relationships and recognition often become measures of success.

But what happens when we achieve these goals and still feel that something is missing? This is one of the central questions explored in It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena, an IAS officer and author. Published by Rupa Publications, the book examines identity, ambition, happiness, relationships, failure and the experiences that shape how we understand ourselves.

Rather than prescribing a universal formula for a meaningful life, Saxena encourages readers to question their assumptions and reflect on what genuinely matters to them.

5 Thought-provoking quotes from the book

1. “Because you can tick every box and still miss your own life.”

This line captures the central message of It Matters A Lot. We often follow a familiar checklist for success, pursuing educational qualifications, professional achievements, financial stability and personal milestones without stopping to question whether these goals reflect our own desires.

The problem is not ambition itself. Working towards something meaningful can bring satisfaction and purpose. However, when our goals are shaped entirely by external expectations, we may lose sight of what makes us happy.

Saxena invites readers to consider whether they are building a life that feels right to them or simply one that looks successful to everyone else.

The lesson: Achievement and fulfilment are not always the same. A meaningful life begins with understanding what success means to you.

2. “You can tick every box and still feel like something is missing.”

This line explores the gap between outward success and inner contentment. A person may have a stable career, a comfortable lifestyle and relationships that appear ideal, yet still struggle to understand why they feel unfulfilled.

Such feelings can arise when we pursue goals without examining the reasons behind them. We may believe that the next promotion, purchase or milestone will finally bring happiness, only to discover that the feeling does not last.

It Matters A Lot encourages readers to look beyond achievements and examine their emotional needs, values and expectations.

The lesson: Before chasing another milestone, pause and ask yourself what you hope it will bring into your life. Sometimes, understanding that desire matters more than achieving the goal.

3. “What happens when everything looks right and still doesn't feel enough?”

This question reflects a familiar struggle in a world that encourages constant comparison. Social media, professional competition and cultural expectations can make us feel that we are falling behind, even when we have made meaningful progress.

The difficulty is that there is always another achievement to pursue and another person against whom to measure ourselves. If our satisfaction depends entirely on reaching the next milestone, contentment can remain perpetually out of reach.

Saxena's book encourages readers to reconsider these expectations and develop a more personal understanding of happiness and fulfilment.

The lesson: You do not have to keep pursuing every goal that society celebrates. Learning to recognise what is enough for you can be just as important as striving for more.

4. “Why do we seek approval?”

The desire for approval can influence our decisions more than we realise. From choosing a career to navigating relationships, we may find ourselves prioritising other people's opinions over our own judgement.

Seeking acceptance is a natural human experience. Problems arise when external validation becomes the primary measure of our worth. We may begin making decisions to avoid criticism rather than to pursue what genuinely matters to us.

By encouraging readers to examine their beliefs and motivations, It Matters A Lot opens the door to greater self-awareness and more conscious choices.

The lesson: Other people's opinions can offer useful perspectives, but they do not have to determine the direction of your life. Understanding your values can help you make decisions with greater confidence.

Also Read
Shubhra Saxena’s It Matters A Lot: 5 Lessons on conscious living
5. “What are we really looking for in love, ambition, happiness, and success?”

These questions bring together several of the themes explored throughout It Matters A Lot. We often pursue different things without examining what we expect them to provide.

We may seek success because we want security, relationships because we want connection, or recognition because we want to feel valued. Yet the things we pursue and the needs we hope to fulfil are not always the same.

Taking time to understand these motivations can help us recognise unhelpful patterns and make choices that better reflect our priorities.

The lesson: Self-awareness begins when we become curious about our own desires. Asking honest questions can help us understand not only what we want, but why we want it.

Final thoughts

It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena invites readers to reconsider the assumptions that shape their understanding of a successful and meaningful life. Its central message is that achievements alone cannot determine whether we feel fulfilled.

Through questions about identity, ambition, relationships and happiness, the book encourages readers to pause and reflect on the lives they are building.

Perhaps the most important question is not whether we have achieved everything we once wanted, but whether the life we are living reflects what truly matters to us.

item.title: FMCG firms grapple with input cost inflation in Q2, brace for margin pressure
item.description: Input-cost pressures intensified in the September quarter, reversing some of the moderation seen in the preceding quarter, which squeezed margins even as companies absorbed part of it to protect consumer demand during the festive season.
item.content:encoded:
FMCG companies face sustained margin pressure in the second half of the current fiscal year, as rising input costs squeeze profitability, with firms weighing post-Diwali price hikes against the risk of hurting consumer demand, particularly in price-sensitive mass-market and rural categories.

Input-cost pressures intensified in the September quarter, reversing some of the moderation seen in the preceding quarter, which squeezed margins even as companies absorbed part of it to protect consumer demand during the festive season.

The increase has been uneven across commodities, with crude-linked derivatives, packaging materials, palm oil and sugar emerging as key pressure points, said Naveen Malpani, Partner and Consumer Industry Leader at Grant Thornton Bharat.

"In rupee terms, palm oil prices were approximately 21% higher year-on-year in September, while sugar prices remained around 18% higher year-on-year despite correcting 8% month-on-month," he said.

Higher costs have not been fully offset by price increases and operational efficiencies, putting pressure on operating margins, Malpani said.

"Pre-results analyst estimates projected operating-margin compression of approximately 45 basis points year-on-year across a group of major consumer staples companies, with some estimates indicating declines of up to 150 basis points for the companies covered," he said.

Companies operating in mass-market categories had limited room for aggressive price increases due to affordability concerns, making cost optimisation, procurement efficiencies and calibrated pricing crucial to protecting profitability without hurting demand.

"The sector should therefore prepare for continued margin pressure through H2, with recovery contingent on actual commodity movements rather than an assumption that the cost cycle has peaked," Malpani added.

Parle Products Chief Marketing Officer Mayank Shah told PTI that rising inflation was a major concern for the FMCG industry, which is "definitely worrisome".

However, he also said companies were trying to absorb a bit of "margin shock" by offsetting higher input costs through efficiency improvements and cost cuts rather than immediately raising prices.

Shah said demand remained robust across urban and rural India as companies refrained from passing on the entire increase in costs to consumers.

However, he indicated that price increases could be considered after the festive season, depending on the movement of agricultural commodity prices and the broader geopolitical situation.

“Most decisions on price hikes would be taken only post festive season… So, you may see some sort of thing happening from December onwards,” Shah said.

Companies are also looking at reducing discounts and advertising expenditure to manage costs, Shah said, adding that protecting demand remained a priority.

Nestle India Chairman and Managing Director Manish Tiwary also acknowledged the issues last week and said "rising inflation, particularly food inflation" is a "reality".

In its commodity outlook, Nestle India said coffee and wheat prices were expected to remain range-bound, while sugar and edible oils would stabilise at elevated levels in the December quarter.

Cocoa remained volatile because of weather-related crop concerns in key producing regions, while milk prices had strengthened seasonally but were expected to ease with the arrival of flush supplies, it said.

Moreover, this inflationary environment poses a challenge for FMCG companies in the second half of FY27, when festive-season demand gives way to the need to sustain consumption momentum and restore profitability.

"Outlook for H2 FY27 remains cautious," said Malpani, adding, " Companies may continue to face cost pressures, with any meaningful margin recovery dependent on commodity prices easing and earlier pricing actions flowing through.

The risk is particularly relevant for packaged foods, home and personal care products and other categories exposed to edible oils, crude derivatives and agricultural commodities.

The potential strengthening of El Niño conditions during October-December also adds uncertainty to the outlook for agricultural production and food prices. Its impact on Indian agriculture, however, will depend on broader ocean-atmosphere conditions and regional weather patterns, and higher food inflation is a risk rather than a certainty.

The impact on consumer demand will be another key factor to watch. While price increases can support value growth, they may not translate into higher underlying volumes if consumers cut purchases, shift to cheaper brands or opt for smaller packs.

“If food inflation rises or rural incomes weaken, consumers may trade down to lower-priced brands, choose smaller packs, reduce purchase frequency or defer discretionary purchases. The uneven monsoon and potential El Niño impact add uncertainty to rural purchasing power,” he said.

item.title: How art platforms, exhibitions and awards strengthen the creative economy
item.description: In this photo essay from Lalit Kala Akademi in New Delhi, we showcase more highlights from an exhibition with 270 artworks from across India.
item.content:encoded:
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,020 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.

Lalit Kala Akademi (LKA) in New Delhi recently hosted its 65th National Exhibition of Art. It showcased over 270 artworks from around the country, selected by a jury from 6,175 submissions.

Twenty artists were also conferred with the Lalit Kala Akademi Awards. The artists include Pooja Rajpoot, Praveen Kumar, Pritam Madhukar Deuskar, Rajendra Prasad, Ramesh Vithal Thorat, Raviram Ramakrishnan, and Sanjay Kumar.

Such exhibitions and awards help transform artistic talent into livelihoods, creative businesses, tourism, and international recognition. By connecting artists with audiences, buyers, institutions, and markets, they strengthen the creative economy while preserving a country’s cultural identity.

Exhibitions provide artists with platforms to showcase, promote and sell their work. They connect creators with the broader ecosystem of collectors, galleries, curators, cultural institutions and potential investors, thus creating opportunities for income generation and professional growth.

In the case of national exhibitions in India, opportunities are also created to showcase traditional crafts, indigenous knowledge, and contemporary artistic practices. Cultural assets thus go beyond elements of nostalgia into sources of sustainable economic value.
